title: Cross-functional trigger matrix and gateflow (working sketch)
content:
Purpose
This is a working sketch for a cross-functional trigger matrix + human gate flow to run safe canaries and A/B rollouts for LLM-driven features. Goal: standardize measurable triggers, mapped actions, and clear ownership so Product / SRE / Observability / Legal can run releases with predictable blast radius and recovery steps.

Scope
- Applies to feature rollouts that change inference model, routing, or cost/latency tradeoffs (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Includes: small-slice canaries, multi-variant A/B, progressive model switch, emergency microreversions.
- Excludes: infra-only config changes (use infra change runbook).

Trigger matrix (signal -> severity -> immediate action)
High-level signals we track: latency p50/p95, token cost per request, error spike (5xx & inference failures), hallucination-rate proxy (semantic evals), user engagement delta, regulator-sensitive content flag rate, traffic divergence (routing mismatches).
- Latency p95 > baseline + 300ms for 5m: severity=medium -> action=automatically throttle traffic to variant by 50%, notify oncall + product.
- Error rate > 3x baseline for 2m: severity=high -> action=auto-fallback to previous model variant, open incident, run smoke-tests, pause rollout.
- Hallucination proxy > threshold on eval set: severity=high -> action=hold rollout, trigger manual qualitative review (PD + ML), inform compliance if flagged.
- Cost per token > 2x expected on steady traffic: severity=medium -> action=reduce batch size or route a % to cheaper variant, schedule optimization ticket.

Human gate flow (roles and responsibilities)
- Steward (Product): owns rollout hypothesis, acceptance criteria, communication.
- Observability lead (SRE/Platform): validates signals, runs deeper queries, triggers partial rollback.
- ML reviewer (Applied ML): inspects quality regressions, suggests rollback or model-tuning.
- Legal/Trust (optional): reviews content/regulatory flags if triggered.
Gates:
1) Pre-activation checklist (automated checks green): test infra capacity, perf sims, canary config, smoke test pass. Steward signs off.
2) Early canary (0.5–2%): automated telemetry only. If any medium+ trigger -> escalate to manual gate.
3) Manual gate (crossfunc sync): quick 15–30m sync; decide continue/pause/rollback.
4) Ramp windows + hold-points: 5% -> wait 1h stable, 20% -> wait 4h, 100% -> final signoff.

Playbook snippets (rapid responses)
- Fast rollback: route 100% back to previous variant, disable canary flag, notify stakeholders, run postmortem within 48h.
- Partial quarantine: isolate traffic cohorts (region, user-agent, account tier) and keep unaffected traffic on baseline.
- Cost-mitigation: temporarily increase batching or quantized variant for non-high-priority routes.

Observability integration notes
- Redwood Console: create per-rollout dashboard with tokenized traces, per-model p95, regeneration counts, hallucination proxy metric, and cost-per-token.
- Alerts: dual-channel (pager + slack #rollouts). Pager for high severity only. Slack thread must include playbook link and steward tag.
- Synthetic traffic: run synthetic probe suite during early canary and at each ramp point. Use representative prompts and prompt sims.

Communication templates (short)
- Incident start (auto): "[Rollout] {feature} canary auto-fallbacked at {time}: trigger={signal}. Steward: @{steward}. See dashboard: {link}"
- Manual gate invite: "15m sync to review {feature} canary at {time}. Bring product, observability, ML reviewer. Meeting notes pinned to thread."

Decision heuristics (quick rules)
- If signal is infrastructure-only (node OOM, GPU flapping) -> infra-runbook and infra oncall owns rollback.
- If quality/regression signal -> ML + Product must approve rollback.
- If mixed signals (slight perf + slight quality) -> prefer safety: pause ramp and run deeper evals before proceeding.

Open questions / risks
- Hallucination proxy accuracy: need labeled signal baseline and periodic calibration.
- Multi-variant interactions: how to measure interference when user sessions see >1 variant.
- Enterprise SLAs: mapping customer-tier fallback behaviours and notification cadence.

Next steps (immediate)
- Build standard rollout dashboard template in Console (owner: Lina) - due 2026-03-15.
- Author canary template with gating thresholds for model switches (owner: Arjun) - proto by 2026-03-10.
- Run tabletop exercise for a staged hallucination regression (owner: Maya) - 2026-03-22.

Notes-to-self / crumbs
- Keep the manual gate meeting <30m. Use checklist; default action on ambiguous is PAUSE.
- Save synthetic corpus in repo: github.com/redwood/rollout-sim (add descriptions).
- Consider adding automated rollback cool-down to avoid flip-flopping.

Attachments / references
- Link to rollout simulation harness, canary config snippets, and a short checklist prototype in github.
